title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business
alternate_titles: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do, and How to Change

contents: Part One — The Habits of Individuals
1: The Habit Loop — How Habits Work
2: The Craving Brain — How to Create New Habits
3: The Golden Rule of Habit Change — Why Transformation Occurs
Part Two — The Habits of Successful Organizations
4: Keystone Habits, or The Ballad of Paul O'Neill — Which Habits Matter Most
5: Starbucks and the Habit of Success — When Willpower Becomes Automatic
6: The Power of a Crisis — How Leaders Create Habits Through Accident and Design
7: How Target Knows What You Want Before You Do — When Companies Predict and Manipulate Habits
Part Three — The Habits of Societies
8: Saddleback Church and the Montgomery Bus Boycott — How Movements Happen
9: The Neurology of Free Will — Are We Responsible for Our Habits?
Appendix: A Reader's Guide to Using These Ideas

audiences: Readers who want a memorable introduction to automatic behaviour and a concrete method for changing one recurring routine
Managers and leaders examining how procedures, incentives, crises, and informal norms shape organisational conduct
People interested in consumer behaviour, marketing ethics, social movements, addiction, or responsibility
Readers who learn well through deeply reported stories and can separate a useful framework from claims that later research has qualified

sources.title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business

sources.supports: Complete text, argument, stories, appendix method, notes, source qualifications, and reading experience.
sources.limitations: Third-party host with uncertain provenance; identity and metadata were cross-checked against publisher and library records.

sources.title: Guides for Using These Ideas
sources.supports: Author-provided habit-change flowcharts and the continuing practical interpretation of the book.
sources.limitations: Promotional companion tools, not independent outcome evidence.

sources.title: MIT researcher sees first evidence that learned behaviors change the brain
sources.supports: Primary-institution account of Graybiel's rat research on striatal activity and behavioural chunking during habit learning.
sources.limitations: Animal maze learning and institutional news summary; not a universal three-step human habit model.

sources.title: Brain researchers explain why old habits die hard
sources.supports: Rat evidence that learned basal-ganglia patterns can quiet when a reward disappears and re-emerge when cues and reward return.
sources.limitations: Animal study; relapse in human behaviour is more varied and context-dependent.

sources.title: Psychology of Habit
sources.author_or_publisher: Wendy Wood and Dennis Rünger; Annual Review of Psychology
sources.supports: Scientific review of habits as context-linked automatic responses, their cognitive and neurobiological properties, and routes to formation and disruption.
sources.limitations: Published after the book and does not test Duhigg's named keystone or organisational frameworks.

sources.title: Habits in everyday life: thought, emotion, and action
sources.author_or_publisher: Wendy Wood, Jeffrey Quinn, and Deborah Kashy; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology via PubMed
sources.supports: Two diary studies showing frequent behaviour in stable contexts is performed with less task-related thought; source of the widely quoted share of daily habitual acts.
sources.limitations: Self-report diaries and a study-specific operational definition; not a fixed percentage for every person.

sources.title: Time to Form a Habit: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Health Behaviour Habit Formation and Its Determinants
sources.author_or_publisher: Ben Singh et al.; Healthcare via PubMed
sources.supports: Current synthesis of health-habit formation, substantial individual variability, importance of repetition, timing, chosen behaviour, pleasure, and context.
sources.limitations: Only twenty studies, most at high risk of bias, and health behaviours dominate.

sources.title: How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world
sources.author_or_publisher: Phillippa Lally et al.; European Journal of Social Psychology, repository record
sources.supports: Daily repetition in the same context and nonlinear growth of automaticity over twelve weeks, with variation by person and behaviour.
sources.limitations: Small self-selected sample, self-report automaticity, and simple health behaviours.

sources.title: Impact of implementation intentions on physical activity practice in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
sources.author_or_publisher: Mariana Bélanger-Gravel et al.; PLOS One
sources.supports: Qualified experimental support for if-then action planning, particularly with reinforcement and obstacle planning, in adult physical activity.
sources.limitations: Small effect, heterogeneous health trials, and not a direct test of the book's complete four-step appendix.

sources.title: A Multisite Preregistered Paradigmatic Test of the Ego-Depletion Effect
sources.author_or_publisher: Kathleen Vohs et al.; Psychological Science via PubMed Central
sources.supports: A 36-lab preregistered test finding no confirmatory evidence for the ego-depletion effect and a very small exploratory estimate.
sources.limitations: Tests selected paradigms; disagreement continues about task strength and the best model of fatigue.

sources.title: Did Target Really Predict a Teen's Pregnancy? The Inside Story
sources.supports: Adversarial reconstruction of the viral Target story, separating the documented prediction project from an anonymous anecdote and later assumptions.
sources.limitations: Industry commentary, not access to Target's model, data, or internal investigation.

sources.title: The Power of Habit
sources.supports: Independent assessment of the loop, cases, diagrams, self-help value, persuasiveness, and simplification.
sources.limitations: Short trade review from publication, not a later evidence audit.

sources.title: MIND Reviews: The Power of Habit
sources.supports: Contemporary science-oriented review of automaticity, the loop, substitution, cases, and broad appeal.
sources.limitations: Brief 2012 review predating later habit syntheses and replication failures.

sources.title: Book review: The Power of Habit
sources.supports: Independent praise for combining serious explanation with entertaining reporting and concise account of the replacement rule.
sources.limitations: Very short positive review without adversarial analysis.

sources.title: The Power of Habit
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for applicability and stories alongside criticism of overinterpretation, repetition, and interrupted narrative structure.
sources.limitations: Self-selected, mutable, and merged across editions; not used in the content rating.

sources.title: Reviews — The Power of Habit
sources.supports: A second reader aggregate with recurring reports of useful application, engaging cases, excessive length, limited neurodivergence coverage, and disproportionate value in the appendix.
sources.limitations: Self-selected and mutable; reviewer expertise and completion are uncontrolled.

workflow.coverage_notes: Complete text and notes checked against publisher and library metadata, author tools, six independent habit and self-control research sources, an adversarial Target analysis, three professional reviews, and two reader aggregates. Later research was used to separate durable context-and-repetition claims from dated ego-depletion and broad case-based claims.
next_steps: Create and time all four content-only narrations, test pronunciation, render local audio, and complete the final quality review.
